claim: Nedd4/Rsp5 family E3 ligases mediate numerous cellular processes, many of which require the E3 ligase to interact with PY motif containing adaptor proteins.
source: Nedd4/Rsp5 family E3 ligases mediate numerous cellular processes, many of which require the E3 ligase to interact with PY motif containing adaptor proteins.
evidence: This is a general statement about Nedd4/Rsp5 E3 ligases that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Several arrestin-related trafficking adaptors (ARTs) of Rsp5 were self-ubiquitinated for activation.
source: Several arrestin-related trafficking adaptors (ARTs) of Rsp5 were self-ubiquitinated for activation, but the regulation mechanism remains elusive.
evidence: This statement references prior knowledge about ART protein ubiquitination but notes the mechanism was previously unclear.

claim: Art1, Art4, and Art5 undergo K63-linked di-ubiquitination by Rsp5.
source: Remarkably, we demonstrate that Art1, Art4, and Art5 undergo K63-linked di-ubiquitination by Rsp5.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Di-ubiquitination of Art1 or Art5 enhances the plasma membrane recruitment of Rsp5 upon substrate induction.
source: This modification enhances the plasma membrane recruitment of Rsp5 by Art1 or Art5 upon substrate induction, required for cargo protein ubiquitination.
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data in Figure 3 showing Rsp5 recruitment to the plasma membrane.

claim: Di-ubiquitin strengthens the interaction between the pombe orthologs of Rsp5 and Art1, Pub1, and Any1.
source: In agreement with these observations, we find that di-ubiquitin strengthens the interaction between the pombe orthologs of Rsp5 and Art1, Pub1, and Any1.
evidence: This is supported by ITC binding data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The HECT domain exosite protects the K63-linked di-ubiquitin on the adaptors from cleavage by the deubiquitination enzyme Ubp2.
source: Furthermore, we discover that the homologous to E6AP C-terminus (HECT) domain exosite protects the K63-linked di-ubiquitin on the adaptors from cleavage by the deubiquitination enzyme Ubp2.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6 showing that deletion of UBP2 rescues adaptor ubiquitination in rsp5-exosite mutants.

claim: Tryptophan-tryptophan (WW) domains of Nedd4 family E3 ligases bind to substrate proteins via interaction with PY motifs containing a consensus sequence P/L-P-x-Y.
source: Tryptophan-tryptophan (WW) domains of Nedd4 family E3 ligases bind to substrate proteins via interaction with PY motifs containing a consensus sequence P/L-P-x-Y (Rotin and Kumar, 2009; Schild et al., 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A family of arrestin-related trafficking adaptors (ARTs) bridge the association between substrates and Rsp5 for ubiquitination.
source: Other substrates lack PY motifs and instead rely on interactions with adaptor proteins that recruit the Nedd4 E3 ligase to them, exemplified by a family of arrestin-related trafficking adaptors (ARTs) that bridge the association between substrates and Rsp5 for ubiquitination (Lin et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lin et al., 2008.

claim: Rsp5 adaptors include a diverse group of proteins to mediate degradation of membrane proteins localized at the PM, Golgi, endosome, and vacuole membrane.
source: Additionally, Rsp5 adaptors include a diverse group of proteins to mediate degradation of membrane proteins localized at the PM, Golgi, endosome, and vacuole membrane (Alvaro et al., 2014; Becuwe et al., 2012; Hatakeyama et al., 2010; Hettema et al., 2004; Hovsepian et al., 2018; Léon et al., 2008; Li et al., 2015; MacDonald et al., 2012; Nikko and Pelham, 2009; O'Donnell et al., 2013; Sardana et al., 2019; Zhu et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The ART proteins Art1, Art4, and Art8 require specific ubiquitination by Rsp5 to reach full activity.
source: The ART proteins Art1, Art4, and Art8 require specific ubiquitination by Rsp5 to reach full activity (Becuwe et al., 2012; Hovsepian et al., 2017; Lin et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Ubiquitination of Nedd4 adaptor protein Commissureless is required to downregulate the Robo receptor at the cell surface of axons, essential for midline crossing.
source: Ubiquitination of Nedd4 adaptor protein Commissureless is required to downregulate the Robo receptor at the cell surface of axons, essential for midline crossing (Ing et al., 2007; Myat et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The N-lobe region of the Nedd4/Rsp5 family E3 ligase HECT domain contains an exosite which binds ubiquitin.
source: The N-lobe region of the Nedd4/Rsp5 family E3 ligase HECT domain contains an exosite which binds ubiquitin (Ub) and has been shown to orient the Ub chain to promote conjugation of the next Ub molecule of the growing polyubiquitin chain (Kim et al., 2011; Maspero et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The HECT domain exosite orients the Ub chain to promote conjugation of the next Ub molecule of the growing polyubiquitin chain.
source: The N-lobe region of the Nedd4/Rsp5 family E3 ligase HECT domain contains an exosite which binds ubiquitin (Ub) and has been shown to orient the Ub chain to promote conjugation of the next Ub molecule of the growing polyubiquitin chain (Kim et al., 2011; Maspero et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Ubiquitinated Rsp5 adaptors are more active when locked onto Rsp5 but less active when unlocked by Ubp2.
source: It was proposed that ubiquitinated Rsp5 adaptors are more active when locked onto Rsp5 but less active when unlocked by Ubp2 (MacDonald et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a proposal from prior literature cited.

claim: At steady state, endogenous Art5 migrates in two major bands by SDS-PAGE, corresponding to the ubiquitinated and non-ubiquitinated species.
source: We found that at steady state, endogenous Art5 migrates in two major bands by SDS-PAGE, corresponding to the ubiquitinated and non-ubiquitinated species (Figure 1B, lane2).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mass spectrometry has previously indicated that Ub is mainly conjugated on the K364 residue of the Art5 α-arrestin domain.
source: Mass spectrometry has previously indicated that Ub is mainly conjugated on the K364 residue of the Art5 α-arrestin domain (Swaney et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior mass spectrometry data.

claim: Art5 ubiquitination is decreased by mutating K364.
source: We confirmed that Art5 ubiquitination was decreased by mutating K364 (Figure 1B, lane 3), and is completely abolished in the art5∆PY mutant in which all three PY motifs (Figure 1A) were mutated (lane 4), demonstrating that Art5 ubiquitination depends on its interaction with Rsp5 via PY motifs.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1B.

claim: Art5 ubiquitination is completely abolished in the art5∆PY mutant in which all three PY motifs were mutated.
source: We confirmed that Art5 ubiquitination was decreased by mutating K364 (Figure 1B, lane 3), and is completely abolished in the art5∆PY mutant in which all three PY motifs (Figure 1A) were mutated (lane 4), demonstrating that Art5 ubiquitination depends on its interaction with Rsp5 via PY motifs.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1B.

claim: Art5 ubiquitination depends on its interaction with Rsp5 via PY motifs.
source: We confirmed that Art5 ubiquitination was decreased by mutating K364 (Figure 1B, lane 3), and is completely abolished in the art5∆PY mutant in which all three PY motifs (Figure 1A) were mutated (lane 4), demonstrating that Art5 ubiquitination depends on its interaction with Rsp5 via PY motifs.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data showing loss of ubiquitination in PY motif mutants.

claim: The ubiquitinated Art5WT runs in line with art5∆PY-2xUb, indicating that Art5 is di-ubiquitinated mainly at the K-364 residue.
source: Remarkably, the ubiquitinated Art5WT runs in line with art5∆PY-2xUb, indicating that Art5 is di-ubiquitinated mainly at the K-364 residue (Figure 1B, lane 4–6).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data comparing migration patterns in Figure 1B.

claim: Rsp5 mainly catalyzed K63-linked Ub chain synthesis in vivo and in vitro.
source: Rsp5 mainly catalyzed K63-linked Ub chain synthesis in vivo and in vitro (Lauwers et al., 2009; Saeki et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The size of the di-ubiquitinated Art5 band is reduced to the mono-ubiquitinated band in the Ub-K63R mutant.
source: Notably, we found that the size of the di-ubiquitinated Art5 band (lanes 2 and 3) is reduced to the mono-ubiquitinated band (lanes 9 and 10), in line with art5∆PY-1xUb (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1C comparing WT and K63R ubiquitin conditions.

claim: Art5 protein is lost in the Ub-K63R mutant in a K364 and PY motif dependent manner.
source: We noticed the loss of Art5 protein in the Ub-K63R mutant in a K364 and PY motif dependent manner (Figure 1C, lane 9), which will be discussed later.
evidence: This is an observation from Western blot data in Figure 1C.

claim: The mono-ubiquitinated band of Art5 in the yeast Ub-K63R mutant is K364 residue dependent.
source: In addition, the mono-ubiquitinated band of Art5 in the yeast Ub-K63R mutant is K364 residue dependent, confirming that the mono-Ub is conjugated mainly at the K364 residue (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1C.

claim: Art5 protein is di-ubiquitinated at the residue K364 in a K63 linkage by Rsp5.
source: Together, our results demonstrate that Art5 protein is di-ubiquitinated at the residue K364 in a K63 linkage by Rsp5.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Art1 contains an N-terminal arrestin fold with PY motifs near its C-terminus and K486 residue is required for Art1 ubiquitination.
source: Art1 contains an N-terminal arrestin fold with PY motifs near its C-terminus and K486 residue is required for Art1 ubiquitination (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the domain architecture shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A and experimental data.

claim: The ubiquitinated form of Art1 shows the same mobility shift in comparison with art1∆PY-2xUb.
source: The ubiquitinated form of Art1 shows the same mobility shift in comparison with art1∆PY-2xUb (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The ubiquitinated band of Art1 migrates with art1∆PY-2xUb in the Ub-WT strain, while Art1 is mono-ubiquitinated at K486 in the yeast strain bearing Ub-K63R.
source: The ubiquitinated band of Art1 migrates with art1∆PY-2xUb in the Ub-WT strain, while Art1 is mono-ubiquitinated at K486 in the yeast strain bearing Ub-K63R (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Art4 interacts with Rsp5 via PY motifs and can be ubiquitinated at a cluster of lysines (235, 245, 264, and 267) in the N-terminal arrestin domain.
source: Art4 interacts with Rsp5 via PY motifs and can be ubiquitinated at a cluster of lysines (235, 245, 264, and 267) in the N-terminal arrestin domain (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by the domain architecture and experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ubiquitinated form of Art4WT migrates with the art4∆PY-2xUb and Art4WT was only mono-ubiquitinated in Ub-K63R condition.
source: The ubiquitinated form of Art4WT migrates with the art4∆PY-2xUb and Art4WT was only mono-ubiquitinated in Ub-K63R condition (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The disappearance of higher molecular weight species of Art1 upon USP2 (non-specific DUB) and AMSH (K63-specific) treatment indicates that the substrate protein Art1 was ubiquitinated with a K63-linked Ub chain.
source: The disappearance of higher molecular weight species of Art1 upon USP2 (non-specific DUB) and AMSH (K63-specific) treatment indicates that the substrate protein Art1 was ubiquitinated with a K63-linked Ub chain.
evidence: This is an inference from the UbiCRest assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Cezanne treatment leads to the better release of the distal-end Ub than the proximal-end Ub from Art1-di-Ub.
source: Intriguingly, Cezanne treatment leads to the better release of the distal-end Ub than the proximal-end Ub from Art1-di-Ub.
evidence: This is an observation from the DUB assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Cezanne removes K63-linked Ub chains, albeit less efficient than hydrolyzing K11-linked Ub chains.
source: This result is consistent with previously published results demonstrating that Cezanne removes K63-linked Ub chains, albeit less efficient than hydrolyzing K11-linked Ub chains (Enesa et al., 2008; Mevissen et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: No cleavage of Art1-di-Ub is visualized when incubated with YOD1, which cleaves K6, K11, K27, K29, or K33 linkage Ub chains.
source: In contrast, no cleavage of Art1-di-Ub is visualized when incubated with YOD1, which cleaves K6, K11, K27, K29, or K33 linkage Ub chains (Mevissen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by DUB assay data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and a citation.

claim: No cleavage of Art1-di-Ub is observed when treated with K48-specific DUB OTUB1.
source: Furthermore, no cleavage of Art1-di-Ub is observed when treated with K48-specific DUB OTUB1 (Mevissen et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2009) and M1-specific DUB OTULIN (Keusekotten et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by DUB assay data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and citations.

claim: No cleavage of Art1-di-Ub is observed when treated with M1-specific DUB OTULIN.
source: Furthermore, no cleavage of Art1-di-Ub is observed when treated with K48-specific DUB OTUB1 (Mevissen et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2009) and M1-specific DUB OTULIN (Keusekotten et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by DUB assay data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A and a citation.

claim: Mono-Ub can be released when K63-linked di-Ub is treated with USP2, AMSH, or Cezanne.
source: In line with the UbiCRest profiling result of Art1 protein (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A), mono-Ub can be released when K63-linked di-Ub is treated with USP2, AMSH, or Cezanne (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is supported by DUB assay data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Art5 is the only ART protein required for the inositol-induced endocytosis and degradation of the PM inositol transporter Itr1.
source: It has been shown that Art5 is the only ART protein required for the inositol-induced endocytosis and degradation of the PM inositol transporter Itr1 (Nikko and Pelham, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Higher inositol concentrations applied for the same amount of time results in more Itr1-GFP degradation in the WT cells and protein sorting into the vacuole lumen.
source: We found that higher inositol concentrations applied for the same amount of time results in more Itr1-GFP degradation in the WT cells and protein sorting into the vacuole lumen (Figure 2A–C) in an Art5 dependent manner.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot and microscopy data in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Itr1-GFP degradation occurs in an Art5 dependent manner.
source: We found that higher inositol concentrations applied for the same amount of time results in more Itr1-GFP degradation in the WT cells and protein sorting into the vacuole lumen (Figure 2A–C) in an Art5 dependent manner.
evidence: This is supported by comparing WT and art5∆ conditions in Figure 2A-C.

claim: The art5K364R mutation causes a severe decrease in the rate of Itr1-GFP degradation compared with Art5WT.
source: The art5K364R caused a severe decrease in the rate of Itr1-GFP degradation (Figure 2A and C) and protein endocytosis (Figure 2B) compared with Art5WT.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot and microscopy data in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Art5 ubiquitination is required to promote efficient Itr1 endocytosis and protein degradation upon inositol-treatment.
source: Thus, Art5 ubiquitination is required to promote efficient Itr1 endocytosis and protein degradation upon inositol-treatment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments comparing Art5WT and art5K364R in Figure 2.

claim: The ubiquitinated pool of Itr1-GFP can be detected in the Art5WT condition, whereas this ubiquitination was attenuated in art5K364R condition.
source: The ubiquitinated pool of Itr1-GFP can be detected in the Art5WT condition, whereas this ubiquitination was attenuated in art5K364R condition (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation and Western blot data in Figure 2D.

claim: The art5K364R can be co-IPed by Itr1-GFP comparable to Art5WT.
source: The art5K364R can be co-IPed by Itr1-GFP comparable to Art5WT, indicating that the decrease of Itrt1 ubiquitination upon inositol stimulation is not due to the loss of interaction between adaptor protein Art5 and cargo protein Itr1.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 2E.

claim: The decrease of Itr1 ubiquitination upon inositol stimulation is not due to the loss of interaction between adaptor protein Art5 and cargo protein Itr1.
source: The art5K364R can be co-IPed by Itr1-GFP comparable to Art5WT, indicating that the decrease of Itrt1 ubiquitination upon inositol stimulation is not due to the loss of interaction between adaptor protein Art5 and cargo protein Itr1.
evidence: This is an inference from the co-IP data showing maintained interaction in Figure 2E.

claim: The art1K486R allele leads to a sorting defect of Mup1-GFP.
source: Consistent with the result of art5K364R, the art1K486R allele leads to a sorting defect of Mup1-GFP (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–1C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot and microscopy data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Mup1 and Art1 interact with each other.
source: Indeed, we can observe the interaction between Mup1 and overexpressed Art1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The Q49R Mup1 mutant does not interact with Art1.
source: In agreement with previous finding that the acidic patch in the Mup1 N-terminal tail is required for binding with Art1 (Guiney et al., 2016), we showed that the Q49R Mup1 mutant does not interact with Art1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E and a citation.

claim: The acidic patch in the Mup1 N-terminal tail is required for binding with Art1.
source: In agreement with previous finding that the acidic patch in the Mup1 N-terminal tail is required for binding with Art1 (Guiney et al., 2016), we showed that the Q49R Mup1 mutant does not interact with Art1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Both Art1WT and art1K486R can bind to Mup1.
source: Furthermore, both Art1WT and art1K486R can bind to Mup1, as evidenced by the Co-IP of art1K486R with Mup1 when Art1 ubiquitination is impaired (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The sorting defect of Mup1-GFP in the presence of art1K486R is not due to the loss of protein interaction between the adaptor protein Art1 and cargo protein Mup1.
source: Thus, our results demonstrate that the sorting defect of Mup1-GFP in the presence of art1K486R is not due to the loss of protein interaction between the adaptor protein Art1 and cargo protein Mup1.
evidence: This is an inference from the co-IP data showing maintained interaction.

claim: TORC1 kinase regulates the Art1-dependent Ub-mediated cargo protein endocytosis by modulating Art1 phosphorylation via Npr1 kinase.
source: Since TORC1 kinase regulates the Art1-dependent Ub-mediated cargo protein endocytosis by modulating Art1 phosphorylation via Npr1 kinase (MacGurn et al., 2011), we next tested if the non-ubiquitinated pool of Art1 altered the Npr1 dependence for phosphorylation, thereby affecting cargo protein sorting.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Both the di-ubiquitinated or the non-ubiquitinated Art1 pools migrated slightly faster in the npr1∆ mutant, consistent with dephosphorylation.
source: We observed that both the di-ubiquitinated or the non-ubiquitinated Art1 pools migrated slightly faster in the npr1∆ mutant, consistent with dephosphorylation (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The activated Npr1 kinase triggered by rapamycin treatment leads to phosphorylation of both Art1WT and art1K486R.
source: Also, the activated Npr1 kinase triggered by rapamycin treatment leads to phosphorylation of both Art1WT and art1K486R, whereas the dephosphorylation of these two proteins is observed following cycloheximide treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Dephosphorylation of Art1WT and art1K486R is observed following cycloheximide treatment.
source: Also, the activated Npr1 kinase triggered by rapamycin treatment leads to phosphorylation of both Art1WT and art1K486R, whereas the dephosphorylation of these two proteins is observed following cycloheximide treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The Npr1-dependent phosphorylation is the intrinsic feature of Art1, regardless of the ubiquitination status of Art1.
source: The Npr1-dependent phosphorylation is therefore the intrinsic feature of Art1, regardless of the ubiquitination status of Art1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The 2xUb fusion does not restore the Itr1 sorting defect in art5K364R and art5∆PY mutants.
source: We first tested if Itr1-GFP sorting can be restored by art5K364R and art5∆PY with C-terminal 2xUb and found the 2xUb fusion does not restore the Itr1 sorting defect (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–3D).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A-D.

claim: The C-terminal Ub fusions to art1K486R or art1∆PY did not enhance their function.
source: We found that the C-terminal Ub fusions to art1K486R or art1∆PY did not enhance their function (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A–4B).
evidence: This is supported by cell growth assay data in Figure 2—figure supplement 4A-B.

claim: Di-Ub needs to be conjugated at specific residues for proper functionality.
source: These results indicate that di-Ub needs to be conjugated at specific residues for proper functionality.
evidence: This is an inference from the experiments showing C-terminal Ub fusions do not rescue function.

claim: The ubiquitination of ARTs is required for enhancing cargo protein sorting but cannot bypass PY motif, responsible for binding with Rsp5.
source: Furthermore, the ubiquitination of ARTs is required for enhancing cargo protein sorting but cannot bypass PY motif, responsible for binding with Rsp5.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments showing PY motif mutants cannot be rescued by Ub fusions.

claim: The Art5WT-GFP localized at cytosol, nucleus, and occasional cytosolic puncta.
source: The Art5WT-GFP localized at cytosol, nucleus, and occasional cytosolic puncta (Sec7-negative, Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3A.

claim: The Art5WT-GFP is re-localized to PM puncta and patch structures after 30 min of inositol (20 µg/mL) treatment.
source: Strikingly, the Art5WT-GFP is re-localized to PM puncta and patch structures after 30 min of inositol (20 µg/mL) treatment.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3B.

claim: The art5K364R-GFP and art5∆PY mainly remain in the cytosol even after inositol treatment.
source: In comparison to Art5WT, the art5K364R-GFP and art5∆PY mainly remain in the cytosol even after inositol treatment (Figure 3B-C).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3B-C.

claim: Rsp5 was observed to be recruited to PM patches after inositol treatment in WT cells.
source: As expected, Rsp5 was observed to be recruited to PM patches after inositol treatment in WT cells.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3D.

claim: Rsp5 PM recruitment after inositol treatment is reduced in cells expressing either art5K364R or art5∆PY.
source: However, Rsp5 PM recruitment after inositol treatment is reduced in cells expressing either art5K364R or art5∆PY (Figure 3D-E).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3D-E.

claim: Art1 is efficiently recruited to the PM in rich medium yeast extract peptone dextrose (YPD) or in minimal medium containing methionine.
source: We found that Art1 is efficiently recruited to the PM in rich medium yeast extract peptone dextrose (YPD) or in minimal medium containing methionine (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The recruitment of art1K486R to the PM is attenuated and no PM recruitment is seen with art1∆PY.
source: In contrast to Art1WT, the recruitment of art1K486R to the PM is attenuated and no PM recruitment is seen with art1∆PY (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–1D).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B-D.

claim: Methionine treatment induces Rsp5 PM recruitment in cells expressing Art1WT, but this recruitment is much reduced in cells expressing art1K486R.
source: As expected, methionine treatment induces Rsp5 PM recruitment in cells expressing Art1WT, but this recruitment is much reduced in cells expressing art1K486R (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–1F).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-F.

claim: The Rsp5 PM recruitment is more significant when overexpressing Art1WT than art1K486R or art1∆PY.
source: In agreement with this data, the Rsp5 PM recruitment is more significant when overexpressing Art1WT than art1K486R or art1∆PY (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G–1H).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1G-H.

claim: Specific ubiquitination of adaptor proteins is required for proper recruitment of Rsp5 to target membranes and subsequent Ub-mediated endocytosis of cargo proteins.
source: Taken together, our results support the model that specific ubiquitination of adaptor proteins is required for proper recruitment of Rsp5 to target membranes and subsequent Ub-mediated endocytosis of cargo proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments in Figure 3 and supplements.

claim: The PM recruitment of Art5-GFP is abolished in the itr1∆ mutant.
source: Strikingly, we found that the PM recruitment of Art5-GFP is abolished in the itr1∆ mutant (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3F-G.

claim: The PM recruitment of Art1 is attenuated in the mup1∆ mutant with methionine induction.
source: Similarly, we observed that the PM recruitment of Art1 is attenuated in the mup1∆ mutant with methionine induction (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–2B).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: Mup1 mutant Q49R is unable to be endocytosed with methionine treatment.
source: Previous data showed that Mup1 mutant Q49R is unable to be endocytosed with methionine treatment (Guiney et al., 2016) and the mup1-Q49R mutation abolishes the protein-protein interaction between Mup1 and Art1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The mup1-Q49R mutation abolishes the protein-protein interaction between Mup1 and Art1.
source: Previous data showed that Mup1 mutant Q49R is unable to be endocytosed with methionine treatment (Guiney et al., 2016) and the mup1-Q49R mutation abolishes the protein-protein interaction between Mup1 and Art1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by co-IP data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: PM recruitment of Art1 is abrogated in the mup1-Q49R condition.
source: We observed that PM recruitment of Art1 is abrogated in the mup1-Q49R condition (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–2B), suggesting that the Mup1-Art1 interaction is required for methionine-induced Art1 PM re-localization.
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-B.

claim: The Mup1-Art1 interaction is required for methionine-induced Art1 PM re-localization.
source: We observed that PM recruitment of Art1 is abrogated in the mup1-Q49R condition (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–2B), suggesting that the Mup1-Art1 interaction is required for methionine-induced Art1 PM re-localization.
evidence: This is an inference from the microscopy data showing loss of Art1 PM recruitment in mup1-Q49R.

claim: The mono-Ub and K63-linked di-Ub bind to GST-HECT domain, but not to GST.
source: The mono-Ub and K63-linked di-Ub chains bind to GST-HECT domain (lane 7), but not to GST (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by GST pull-down assay data in Figure 4A.

claim: The binding between mono-Ub and HECT domain depends on the exosite/Ub interface (Y516 and F618).
source: The binding between mono-Ub and HECT domain depends on the exosite/Ub interface (Y516 and F618) (French et al., 2009; Kim et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The binding between K63-linked di-Ub and HECT domain is disrupted by the exosite mutants Y516A, F618A, or the Y516A/F618A double mutant.
source: We found that the binding between K63-linked di-Ub and HECT domain is disrupted by the exosite mutants Y516A, F618A, or the Y516A/F618A double mutant (lanes 8–10, Figure 4A), suggesting that the K63-linked di-Ub also interacts with the HECT domain via the exosite.
evidence: This is supported by GST pull-down assay data in Figure 4A.

claim: The K63-linked di-Ub interacts with the HECT domain via the exosite.
source: We found that the binding between K63-linked di-Ub and HECT domain is disrupted by the exosite mutants Y516A, F618A, or the Y516A/F618A double mutant (lanes 8–10, Figure 4A), suggesting that the K63-linked di-Ub also interacts with the HECT domain via the exosite.
evidence: This is an inference from the GST pull-down data showing loss of binding in exosite mutants.

claim: The dissociation constant (Kd) for the interaction between HECT and mono-Ub is approximately 201 µM.
source: The dissociation constant (Kd) for the interaction between HECT and mono-Ub was quantified by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) assay to be approximately 201 µM (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by ITC data in Figure 4B.

claim: The I44A mutation of Ub abolishes the binding between mono-Ub and the HECT domain.
source: As expected, the I44A mutation of Ub abolishes the binding between mono-Ub and the HECT domain (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by ITC data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The HECT domain exosite and the I44-containing Ub hydrophobic surface are required to bridge the protein-protein interaction between the HECT domain and ubiquitin.
source: Our results suggest that the HECT domain exosite and the I44-containing Ub hydrophobic surface are required to bridge the protein-protein interaction between the HECT domain and ubiquitin.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ITC and GST pull-down experiments.

claim: K63-linked di-Ub enhances the HECT domain binding affinity (Kd = 33 µM), nearly sixfold relative to the mono-Ub.
source: In contrast to the mono-Ub results, K63-linked di-Ub enhances the HECT domain binding affinity (Kd = 33 µM), nearly sixfold relative to the mono-Ub (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by ITC data in Figure 4C.

claim: M1-linked di-Ub was proposed to mimic the K63 Ub linkage.
source: Head-to-tail M1-linked di-Ub was proposed to mimic the K63 Ub linkage (Komander et al., 2009; Zhu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: M1-linked di-Ub binds to HECT with Kd = 36 µM, comparable with the K63-linked di-Ub.
source: As expected, our ITC analysis showed that M1-linked di-Ub binds to HECT with Kd = 36 µM (Figure 4D), comparable with the K63-linked di-Ub.
evidence: This is supported by ITC data in Figure 4D.

claim: The binding between GST-2xUb and HECT domain is stronger than GST-Ub.
source: Also, our in-vitro binding assay showed that the binding between GST-2xUb and HECT domain is stronger than GST-Ub (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by GST pull-down assay data in Figure 4E.

claim: K48-linked di-Ub shows a much lower affinity than K63-di-Ub, Kd = 145 µM.
source: In comparison, K48-linked di-Ub shows a much lower affinity than K63-di-Ub, Kd = 145 µM (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by ITC data in Figure 4F.

claim: No binding was detected between the Ub variants and exosite mutant F618A.
source: In line with the GST-binding result (Figure 4A), no binding was detected between the Ub variants and exosite mutant F618A (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-E).
evidence: This is supported by ITC data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B-E.

claim: HECT domain specifically binds to linear form K63-linked di-Ub and the exosite site is required for Ub binding.
source: Thus, our results demonstrate that HECT domain specifically binds to linear form K63-linked di-Ub and the exosite site is required for Ub binding.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ITC and GST pull-down experiments.

claim: The K63-linked UbWT-UbI44A binds to HECT with a Kd = 120 µM, lower binding affinity than the K63 di-Ub.
source: We found that the K63-linked UbWT-UbI44A binds to HECT with a Kd = 120 µM, lower binding affinity than the K63 di-Ub (Figure 4G, Figure 4—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by ITC data in Figure 4G and Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Both distal and proximal ubiquitins contribute to the HECT domain binding.
source: Together, our result suggests that both distal and proximal ubiquitins contribute to the HECT domain binding.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ITC experiments with distal end I44A mutant.

claim: Art1 and Art5 PY motif containing peptides interact with purified WW domains from Rsp5 (Kd = 3.6 µM for Art1, Kd = 3.1 µM for Art5).
source: Indeed, Art1 and Art5 PY motif containing peptides interact with purified WW domains from Rsp5 (Kd = 3.6 µM for Art1, Kd = 3.1 µM for Art5), but not with PY motif mutants (Figure 5C-D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–1B).
evidence: This is supported by ITC data in Figure 5C-D.

claim: Art1 and Art5 PY motif mutants do not interact with purified WW domains from Rsp5.
source: Indeed, Art1 and Art5 PY motif containing peptides interact with purified WW domains from Rsp5 (Kd = 3.6 µM for Art1, Kd = 3.1 µM for Art5), but not with PY motif mutants (Figure 5C-D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–1B).
evidence: This is supported by ITC data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-B.

claim: The S. pombe Rsp5 ortholog Pub1 interacts with Any1 with a binding affinity Kd~2.1 µM.
source: The S. pombe Rsp5 ortholog Pub1 interacts with Any1 with a binding affinity Kd~2.1 µM (Figure 5E), in a similar range as the binding affinity between PY motifs and WW domains shown earlier (Figure 5C-D).
evidence: This is supported by ITC data in Figure 5E.

claim: Any1 can be co-fractionated with Pub1 without being conjugated with di-Ub.
source: The association between Pub1 and Any1 was also demonstrated by size exclusion chromatography, in which the Any1 can be co-fractionated with Pub1 without being conjugated with di-Ub (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–2C).
evidence: This is supported by size exclusion chromatography data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Pub1 interacts with Any1 in a PY motif dependent manner.
source: The ITC and co-fractionation results suggest that Pub1 interacts with Any1 in a PY motif dependent manner.
evidence: This is an inference from the ITC and size exclusion chromatography data.

claim: Any1 conjugated with K63 di-Ub enhances the binding with Pub1 nearly eightfold in comparison with non-conjugated Any1.
source: Remarkably, Any1 conjugated with K63 di-Ub enhances the binding with Pub1 nearly eightfold in comparison with non-conjugated Any1 (Figure 5F), suggesting that di-Ub conjugation onto Any1 probably leads to a structural conformation change of Any1 and therefore enhances the Pub1 binding.
evidence: This is supported by ITC data in Figure 5F.

claim: Di-Ub conjugation onto Any1 probably leads to a structural conformation change of Any1 and therefore enhances the Pub1 binding.
source: Remarkably, Any1 conjugated with K63 di-Ub enhances the binding with Pub1 nearly eightfold in comparison with non-conjugated Any1 (Figure 5F), suggesting that di-Ub conjugation onto Any1 probably leads to a structural conformation change of Any1 and therefore enhances the Pub1 binding.
evidence: This is speculation based on the enhanced binding observed in ITC experiments.

claim: The Any1-di-Ub binds to exosite mutant pub1-F576A with a Kd = 2.3 µM.
source: In comparison, the Any1-di-Ub binds to exosite mutant pub1-F576A with a Kd = 2.3 µM (Figure 5G), confirming that the di-Ub binds to Pub1 exosite.
evidence: This is supported by ITC data in Figure 5G.

claim: The di-Ub binds to Pub1 exosite.
source: In comparison, the Any1-di-Ub binds to exosite mutant pub1-F576A with a Kd = 2.3 µM (Figure 5G), confirming that the di-Ub binds to Pub1 exosite.
evidence: This is confirmed by comparing binding affinities with WT and exosite mutant Pub1.

claim: The di-ubiquitination of adaptor proteins enhances the binding affinity with the E3 ligase, leading to E3 ligase recruitment and cargo protein ubiquitination and sorting.
source: Together, the di-ubiquitination of adaptor proteins enhances the binding affinity with the E3 ligase, leading to E3 ligase recruitment and cargo protein ubiquitination and sorting.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ITC and functional experiments.

claim: The di-ubiquitinated form of Art5 is diminished in the rsp5-F618A mutant.
source: The di-ubiquitinated form of Art5 is diminished in the rsp5-F618A mutant (Figure 6A, lane 3).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6A.

claim: The di-ubiquitinated pool of Art1 is substantially attenuated in either the Y516A or F618A exosite mutant.
source: Similarly, the di-ubiquitinated pool of Art1 is substantially attenuated in either the Y516A or F618A exosite mutant (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Exosite mutants do not alter the binding affinity between E3 and E2 enzymes, the transthiolation process from E2 to E3, or the self-ubiquitination activity of Nedd4.
source: It was reported that exosite mutants do not alter the binding affinity between E3 and E2 enzymes, the transthiolation process from E2 to E3, or the self-ubiquitination activity of Nedd4 (Maspero et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Overexpressing UBP2 leads to a reduction of the di-ubiquitinated Art1.
source: To test it, we performed a multicopy gene suppression screen with yeast DUBs and found that overexpressing UBP2 leads to a reduction of the di-ubiquitinated Art1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The di-Ub modification of Art1 is restored when the catalytic dead mutant C745V of Ubp2 is overexpressed.
source: Furthermore, the di-Ub modification of Art1 is restored when the catalytic dead mutant C745V of Ubp2 is overexpressed (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Ubp2 may function as a DUB to trim the di-ubiquitinated form of Rsp5 adaptor proteins.
source: This result infers that Ubp2 may function as a DUB to trim the di-ubiquitinated form of Rsp5 adaptor proteins.
evidence: This is an inference from the experiments showing Ubp2 overexpression reduces adaptor di-ubiquitination.

claim: The di-ubiquitinated Art5 and Art1 are nearly fully restored in the rsp5-F618A/ubp2∆ strain.
source: Strikingly, the di-ubiquitinated Art5 and Art1 are nearly fully restored in the rsp5-F618A/ubp2∆ strain (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), indicating that Ubp2 trims the di-Ub on adaptors Art5 and Art1 when they are disengaged from the Rsp5 exosite.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Ubp2 trims the di-Ub on adaptors Art5 and Art1 when they are disengaged from the Rsp5 exosite.
source: Strikingly, the di-ubiquitinated Art5 and Art1 are nearly fully restored in the rsp5-F618A/ubp2∆ strain (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), indicating that Ubp2 trims the di-Ub on adaptors Art5 and Art1 when they are disengaged from the Rsp5 exosite.
evidence: This is an inference from the rescue of di-ubiquitination in the double mutant.

claim: The Ubp2-WT abrogates the rescue of Art1 trimming seen in the rsp5-F618A/ubp2∆ double mutant, whereas the ubp2-C745V does not.
source: We found that the Ubp2-WT abrogates the rescue of Art1 trimming seen in the lane 1, whereas the ubp2-C745V does not (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The exosite can protect the di-Ub moiety on adaptors from the cleavage by Ubp2.
source: Together, these results suggest that the exosite can protect the di-Ub moiety on adaptors from the cleavage by Ubp2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments showing rescue in exosite/ubp2 double mutants.

claim: The full length Art5 protein is restored 3.8-fold upon the inhibition of proteasome function by MG132.
source: We found that the full length Art5 protein is restored 3.8-fold upon the inhibition of proteasome function by MG132 (Figure 6B), suggesting that Art5 probably undergoes K48-linked polyubiquitination because K48-linked Ub chains are preferred by proteasome.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6B.

claim: Art5 probably undergoes K48-linked polyubiquitination because K48-linked Ub chains are preferred by proteasome.
source: We found that the full length Art5 protein is restored 3.8-fold upon the inhibition of proteasome function by MG132 (Figure 6B), suggesting that Art5 probably undergoes K48-linked polyubiquitination because K48-linked Ub chains are preferred by proteasome.
evidence: This is speculation based on the proteasome inhibitor rescue and established knowledge about K48 chains.

claim: Either the PY motif or the K364R mutant rescues the loss of Art5.
source: Either the PY motif or the K364R mutant rescues the loss of Art5 (Figure 6B), indicating that Rsp5 is responsible for Art5 degradation and the K364 is used for this ubiquitination process.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6B.

claim: Rsp5 is responsible for Art5 degradation and the K364 is used for this ubiquitination process.
source: Either the PY motif or the K364R mutant rescues the loss of Art5 (Figure 6B), indicating that Rsp5 is responsible for Art5 degradation and the K364 is used for this ubiquitination process.
evidence: This is an inference from the rescue experiments with PY and K364R mutants.

claim: Expressing myc-Ub K63R does not affect Art5 hyperubiquitination in the rsp5-exosite mutant background, whereas the K48R Ub mutant substantially reduced Art5 ubiquitination.
source: We found that expressing myc-Ub K63R does not affect Art5 hyperubiquitination in the rsp5-exosite mutant background, whereas the K48R Ub mutant substantially reduced Art5 ubiquitination (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by immunoprecipitation and Western blot data in Figure 6C.

claim: The Art5 ubiquitination in the rsp5-exosite mutant is mediated by a K48-linked polyubiquitin chain.
source: This result suggests that the Art5 ubiquitination in the rsp5-exosite mutant is mediated by a K48-linked polyubiquitin chain.
evidence: This is an inference from the experiments with K48R ubiquitin mutant.

claim: Art5 protein is also degraded in the Ub-K63R mutant.
source: We observed that Art5 protein is also degraded in the Ub-K63R mutant (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an observation from Western blot data in Figure 1C.

claim: ubp2∆ does not reverse the loss of Art5 protein in the Ub-K63R mutant.
source: To test this, we deleted Ubp2 in the Ub-K63R mutant and found that ubp2∆ does not reverse the loss of Art5 protein (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6D.

claim: The loss of K63-linked di-Ub on Art5, instead of Ubp2, in either the Ub-K63R mutant or rsp5-exosite mutant, leads to Art5 degradation.
source: Our results suggest that the loss of K63-linked di-Ub on Art5, instead of Ubp2, in either the Ub-K63R mutant or rsp5-exosite mutant, leads to Art5 degradation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments in Figure 6D.

claim: The Art5 degradation can be rescued in art5-K364R and art5-∆PY mutant in the Ub-K63R and rsp5-exosite conditions.
source: Also, in these two conditions, the Art5 degradation can be rescued in art5-K364R and art5-∆PY mutant (Figure 6B and D).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6B and D.

claim: Pre-existing Art5 or Art1 undergoes ubiquitination upon inositol or methionine treatment for 1 hr in both WT and ubp2∆ conditions.
source: As seen in the Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–2D, pre-existing Art5 or Art1 undergoes ubiquitination upon inositol or methionine treatment for 1 hr in both WT and ubp2∆ conditions, whereas the adaptor proteins shifted back to less ubiquitinated status after removing the stimulation in the WT condition, but not in the ubp2∆ mutant.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-D.

claim: The adaptor proteins shifted back to less ubiquitinated status after removing the stimulation in the WT condition, but not in the ubp2∆ mutant.
source: As seen in the Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–2D, pre-existing Art5 or Art1 undergoes ubiquitination upon inositol or methionine treatment for 1 hr in both WT and ubp2∆ conditions, whereas the adaptor proteins shifted back to less ubiquitinated status after removing the stimulation in the WT condition, but not in the ubp2∆ mutant.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-D.

claim: Stimulation enhances adaptor ubiquitination.
source: First, stimulation enhances adaptor ubiquitination.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the tet-Off experiments in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The ubiquitinated pool of adaptor proteins can be deubiquitinated by Ubp2 when stimulation is terminated.
source: Second, the ubiquitinated pool of adaptor proteins can be deubiquitinated by Ubp2 when stimulation is terminated.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the tet-Off experiments in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: K63-linked di-Ub activates Rsp5 function.
source: First, K63-linked di-Ub activates Rsp5 function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the functional and binding experiments throughout the study.

claim: K63-linked di-Ub enables the full engagement of adaptors onto the Rsp5 exosite and sharply enhances the binding affinity with Rsp5.
source: K63-linked di-Ub enables the full engagement of adaptors onto the Rsp5 exosite and sharply enhances the binding affinity with Rsp5, which facilitates Rsp5 recruitment and accelerates substrate protein ubiquitination.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the ITC and functional experiments.

claim: K63-linked di-Ub on adaptors engaged with the Rsp5 exosite are not accessible to Ubp2.
source: Second, K63-linked di-Ub on adaptors engaged with the Rsp5 exosite are not accessible to Ubp2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments showing rescue in exosite/ubp2 double mutants.

claim: Once released from Rsp5 exosite, the exposed K63-linked di-Ub is subjected to cleavage by Ubp2.
source: Once released from Rsp5 exosite, the exposed K63-linked di-Ub is subjected to cleavage by Ubp2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments showing Ubp2-dependent deubiquitination.

claim: Adaptor proteins undergo ubiquitination upon substrate stimulation and Ubp2 is required for DUB of adaptor proteins once the stimulation is removed.
source: Using tet-Off system, we have shown that adaptor proteins undergo ubiquitination upon substrate stimulation and Ubp2 is required for DUB of adaptor proteins once the stimulation is removed.
evidence: This is supported by the tet-Off experiments in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ubiquitinated adaptor proteins were deubiquitinated by Ubp2 so that the adaptor proteins can be recycled for the next round of ubiquitination event.
source: As hypothesized by our earlier review (MacGurn et al., 2012), our current data supports the model that ubiquitinated adaptor proteins were deubiquitinated by Ubp2 so that the adaptor proteins can be recycled for the next round of ubiquitination event.
evidence: This is a model supported by the current data and a prior hypothesis.

claim: The interaction between the di-Ub chain and the HECT domain locks the E3 ligase and adaptor into an active/functional conformation.
source: We reason that the interaction between the di-Ub chain and the HECT domain locks the E3 ligase and adaptor into an active/functional conformation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the binding and functional data.

claim: The Nedd4/Rsp5 ligase exosite is required for efficient Ub conjugation for adaptor-independent ubiquitination.
source: For adaptor-independent ubiquitination, the Nedd4/Rsp5 ligase exosite is also required for efficient Ub conjugation, demonstrating that the 'Ub-exosite binding' is required to localize and orient the distal-end Ub chain to promote conjugation (Kim et al., 2011; Maspero et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The binding between 'di-Ub and exosite' not only enhances the binding affinity between the E3 ligase and adaptor but also leads to more productive Rsp5 recruitment to properly orient and present the substrate for ubiquitination at target membranes.
source: In terms of the Rsp5 adaptor-mediated function, we propose that the binding between 'di-Ub and exosite' not only enhances the binding affinity between the E3 ligase and adaptor (Figure 5E, F), but also leads to more productive Rsp5 recruitment to properly orient and present the substrate for ubiquitination at target membranes.
evidence: This is a proposal based on the binding and functional data.

claim: K63 di-Ub generates a sixfold tighter binding to the HECT domain than mono-Ub.
source: While we presented the evidence of E3 ligase activation by ubiquitinated adaptors, we also showed that K63 di-Ub generates a sixfold tighter binding to the HECT domain than mono-Ub.
evidence: This is supported by ITC data comparing mono-Ub and K63 di-Ub binding.

claim: The K63 di-Ub not only provides alternative options to bind a single site, but also fits with a model in which there are multiple Ub binding sites.
source: We reason that the K63 di-Ub not only provides alternative options to bind a single site, but also fits with a model in which there are multiple Ub binding sites.
evidence: This is speculation based on the binding data and prior structural knowledge.

claim: Three N-lobe mutations (Y516A, F618A, and V621A/V622A) completely abolished Ub binding and three extra mutations (N513A, Y521A, and R651A) caused a reduction in binding.
source: It was found that three N-lobe mutations (Y516A, F618A, and V621A/V622A) completely abolished Ub binding and three extra mutations (N513A, Y521A, and R651A) caused a reduction in binding (French et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The L8-I44-V70 hydrophobic patch of mono-Ub sits on Rsp5 in three legs, like a tripod.
source: Kim and coworkers found that the L8-I44-V70 hydrophobic patch of mono-Ub sits on Rsp5 in three legs, like a tripod (Kim et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Two separated UIMs in Rap80 bind to extended K63-linked Ub chain favorably.
source: Likewise, two separated UIMs in Rap80 bind to extended K63-linked Ub chain favorably (Sato et al., 2009; Sims and Cohen, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Rsp5 exosite accommodates the two hydrophobic patches of the distal and proximal Ub at multiple Ub binding sites.
source: We propose that Rsp5 exosite accommodates the two hydrophobic patches of the distal and proximal Ub at multiple Ub binding sites, which needs be assigned in the future by structural analysis.
evidence: This is a proposal that requires future structural studies.

claim: Short K63 di-Ub chains (<4) generally do not play as degradation signal.
source: While the K63-linked di-Ub binds to the HECT domain with a stronger affinity than K48-linked di-Ub (Figure 4), short K63 di-Ub chains (<4) generally do not play as degradation signal (Nathan et al., 2013; Thrower et al., 2000; Windecker and Ulrich, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Both the M1- and K63-linked di-Ub adopt an equivalent open conformation.
source: Interestingly, both the M1- and K63-linked di-Ub adopt an equivalent open conformation (Komander et al., 2009) and exhibit similar binding affinity to the HECT domain (Figure 4), indicating that the HECT domain exosite has a strong preference for the linear and extended form of di-Ub.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature and ITC data.

claim: The HECT domain exosite has a strong preference for the linear and extended form of di-Ub.
source: Interestingly, both the M1- and K63-linked di-Ub adopt an equivalent open conformation (Komander et al., 2009) and exhibit similar binding affinity to the HECT domain (Figure 4), indicating that the HECT domain exosite has a strong preference for the linear and extended form of di-Ub.
evidence: This is an inference from the similar binding affinities of M1 and K63 di-Ub.

claim: The K48-linked polyubiquitin chain adopts a significantly distinct and compact structure.
source: In contrast, the K48-linked polyubiquitin chain adopts a significantly distinct and compact structure (Eddins et al., 2007), which may not be favorable for the HECT domain.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The K48-linked polyubiquitin chain structure may not be favorable for the HECT domain.
source: In contrast, the K48-linked polyubiquitin chain adopts a significantly distinct and compact structure (Eddins et al., 2007), which may not be favorable for the HECT domain.
evidence: This is speculation based on structural differences and binding data.

claim: The K63-linked Ub chains (≥3) likely generate stronger binding with the HECT domain than di-Ub.
source: On the one hand, this probably correlates with the physiological reversible function of adaptors. The K63-linked Ub chains (≥3) likely generate stronger binding with the HECT domain than di-Ub.
evidence: This is speculation based on the binding data for di-Ub.

claim: The di-Ub binds well with HECT domain, but still can be disengaged from the HECT domain under physiological conditions so that Rsp5 can be disassociated and recycled.
source: We reason that the di-Ub binds well with HECT domain, but still can be disengaged from the HECT domain under physiological conditions so that Rsp5 can be disassociated and recycled.
evidence: This is speculation about the physiological significance of the binding affinity.

claim: The K63-linked di-Ub is probably just enough to be masked by the HECT domain exosite cavity whereas longer chains will be trimmed by Ubp2.
source: Furthermore, the K63-linked di-Ub is probably just enough to be masked by the HECT domain exosite cavity whereas longer chains will be trimmed by Ubp2.
evidence: This is speculation about the mechanism of chain length control.

claim: An adaptor should disassociate from Rsp5 to allow other adaptors to engage with Rsp5 to ubiquitinate different substrate proteins.
source: The PY motif containing Rsp5 adaptors share the E3 ligase Rsp5 and an adaptor should disassociate from Rsp5 to allow other adaptors to engage with Rsp5 to ubiquitinate different substrate proteins.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the need for adaptor recycling.

claim: Nedd4-mediated downregulation of the sodium channel ENaC is impaired when Nedd4 is sequestered by overexpression of another Nedd4 E3 adaptor, Ndfip2.
source: In agreement with this working model, Nedd4-mediated downregulation of the sodium channel ENaC is impaired when Nedd4 is sequestered by overexpression of another Nedd4 E3 adaptor, Ndfip2 (Konstas et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Ubp2 allows the recycling of Rsp5 from its adaptor proteins.
source: Besides cleavage of K63 di-Ub in the rsp5-exosite mutant, Ubp2 allows the recycling of Rsp5 from its adaptor proteins.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments showing Ubp2-dependent deubiquitination.

claim: Several Rsp5 adaptors compete for Rsp5 and a Ubp2 deficiency increased both the adaptor activity and the ability to compete for Rsp5.
source: MacDonald and coworkers proposed that several Rsp5 adaptors compete for Rsp5 and a Ubp2 deficiency increased both the adaptor activity and the ability to compete for Rsp5 (MacDonald et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a proposal from prior literature cited.

claim: Art5 and Art1 di-ubiquitination in response to inositol or methionine treatment is inhibited in the absence of Ubp2.
source: Indeed, we observe that Art5 and Art1 di-ubiquitination in response to inositol or methionine treatment is inhibited in the absence of Ubp2 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), indicating the decrease of Rsp5 availability in ubp2∆ mutant.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The decrease of Rsp5 availability occurs in ubp2∆ mutant.
source: Indeed, we observe that Art5 and Art1 di-ubiquitination in response to inositol or methionine treatment is inhibited in the absence of Ubp2 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), indicating the decrease of Rsp5 availability in ubp2∆ mutant.
evidence: This is an inference from the reduced adaptor ubiquitination in ubp2∆.

claim: K63 di-Ub greatly enhances the binding affinity between adaptors and E3 ligase.
source: Since K63 di-Ub greatly enhances the binding affinity between adaptors and E3 ligase, Ubp2 likely helps the Nedd4/Rsp5 E3 ligase to catalyze distinct ubiquitination events by cleaving the di-Ub off the adaptors and recycling Rsp5.
evidence: This is supported by ITC data showing enhanced binding.

claim: Ubp2 likely helps the Nedd4/Rsp5 E3 ligase to catalyze distinct ubiquitination events by cleaving the di-Ub off the adaptors and recycling Rsp5.
source: Since K63 di-Ub greatly enhances the binding affinity between adaptors and E3 ligase, Ubp2 likely helps the Nedd4/Rsp5 E3 ligase to catalyze distinct ubiquitination events by cleaving the di-Ub off the adaptors and recycling Rsp5.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the functional and biochemical data.

claim: Activated Rsp5 can be released from engaged adaptor proteins.
source: The multitasking of Rsp5 via various adaptors leads us to hypothesize that activated Rsp5 can be released from engaged adaptor proteins.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the multitasking nature of Rsp5.

claim: The adaptor proteins Art1 and Art5 undergo di-ubiquitination upon environmental stimulation and Ubp2 is required to reverse this ubiquitination.
source: We showed that the adaptor proteins Art1 and Art5 undergo di-ubiquitination upon environmental stimulation and Ubp2 is required to reverse this ubiquitination.
evidence: This is supported by the tet-Off experiments in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Once the ubiquitination is done, the engaged K63 di-Ub is exposed for cleavage by Ubp2.
source: Once the ubiquitination is done, the engaged K63 di-Ub is exposed for cleavage by Ubp2.

claim: Ubp2 acts on ubiquitinated adaptor proteins to release the adaptor proteins and Rsp5.
